title: TDD with Jest and Pytest
summary: Test-Driven Development: write a failing test first, make it pass, then clean up (Red → Green → Refactor), using Pytest for Python and Jest for JavaScript, and running tests in Docker. The step-by-step arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Write a failing test, make it pass, and refactor, in both Pytest and Jest, and read test output to fix a failure.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Skim Intro to TDD with PyTest and TDD with Jest. Note how each finds test files (test_*.py vs *.test.js) and how assertions look (assert x == y vs expect(x).toBe(y)).
steps.doneWhen: You can describe Red → Green → Refactor and name each tool's test-file pattern.

steps.title: See tests you already have
steps.detail: Myflix already has tests: Vitest, which uses the same describe/it/expect style as Jest. Run them to see a passing suite's output.
steps.doneWhen: You see the passing test count and can open one file in src/test/ and read what it checks.

steps.title: Set up pytest in a throwaway folder
steps.detail: Use a virtual environment so pytest doesn't touch the system Python. Write one test that fails, then make it pass.
steps.code:
mkdir -p ~/tmp-tdd && cd ~/tmp-tdd
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install pytest
printf 'def add(a, b):
    return 0

def test_add():
    assert add(2, 3) == 5
' > test_add.py
pytest   # red: fix add() and run again for green
steps.doneWhen: pytest shows 1 failed, then 1 passed after your fix.

steps.title: Note the listed assignments
steps.detail: The curriculum lists Part I: Roman Numerals (Python) and Linear Search (Python). Part II: Fibonacci, Linear Search (JS) and Test my Calculator (intro-to-pytest). Wait for Slack to confirm. The /tdd skill can coach you through red-green-refactor.
steps.doneWhen: You know which repos to expect.

concepts.meaning: Write the test before the code, so the test describes what "done" means.
See the test fail, write just enough code to pass, then tidy up while tests stay green.
A line that checks a result and fails the test if it's wrong.
The test runners for Python / JavaScript.
The number a command returns: 0 means all tests passed. CI uses it to pass or fail a build.
